terms.grammar: noun, third declension, with an adjective
evidence: Caes. BC 1.52: nōn sōlum inopiā praesentis, sed etiam futūrī temporis (Lewis & Short)
Hor. C. 3.29.29: prūdēns futūrī temporis exitum (Lewis & Short)
Plaut. Men. 4.3.21: aliam posthāc invenītō (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Fam. 2.8.1: longē in posterum prōspicere (Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: tempora autem reī pūblicae quālia futūra sint quis scit? mihi quidem turbulenta videntur fore
phrases.english: but who knows what the political future holds? To me it looks stormy

phrases.latin: dum loquimur, fūgerit invida aetās: carpe diem, quam minimum crēdula posterō
phrases.english: while we talk, envious time will have fled: seize the day, and trust as little as you can to the future

sources: Lewis & Short: tempus · Lewis & Short: futurus · Lewis & Short: posthac · Lewis & Short: posterus
